Urgent funding for research into Long Covid and ME/CFS treatments and cures, Around a quarter of a million people are suffering with ME/CFS in the UK and over 2 million with long Covid. Many of these people are severely disabled. There are no cures of specific medicines for these conditions. Urgent funding is needed for research to find effective treatments and cures., It is quite frankly a disgrace that so little funding has gone into ME/CFS in the past few decades. The new pandemic is long Covid and we believe sufferers are not receiving enough help due to lack of research into treatments and cures. We need urgent funding for research into the pathology of these conditions. This should include research into mitochondria and the autonomic nervous system of patients with these conditions.
 
Millions of people are missing out on their lives. The Government must act now.

Pause the Covid-19 vaccination programme in England, We believe England's COVID-19 vaccination programme should be paused due to the potential risks associated with these vaccines. It is important for the UK Government to conduct and publish a comprehensive risk-benefit analysis for open peer review before continuing the vaccination program., The number of COVID-19 hospitalizations and patients in hospitals have both decreased significantly since the pandemic's peak. Given this decease, the risk-benefit analysis of the vaccination program has changed.

Cancel plans for "maths to 18", We want the Government to abandon plans to ensure that all school pupils in England study some form of maths to the age of 18., We want students to be able to choose what subjects they study after they complete their GCSEs.
 
Because many children have ambitions that do not require advanced maths. We believe GCSE maths is sufficient education, and if a child would like to continue maths into college then that should be their choice, not the Government’s.

Require landlords to supply references from past tenants, For references from past tenants to be supplied by every landlord before a new tenant moves into a property. The Government should put in place measures to ensure that references are genuine., I have personally been effected by moving into flats that had on going / known issues that hadn’t been sorted before moving in.

Remove LGBT content from the Relationships Education curriculum, We believe kids shouldn't learn about this at an early age. I am sure there are many parents who do not want their or other children taught about LGBT in primary school.,

Guarantee access to broadcast TV (Freeview) and aerial radio beyond 2040, The Government must guarantee access to Freeview and aerial radio beyond 2040. Unless the Government takes such action ahead of the World Radiocommunication Conference in November 2023 the spectrum of frequency allocated to Digital Terrestrial TV (Freeview) may be lost and the services disbanded, Millions rely on Freeview/broadcast TV and radio to keep in touch with society. Silver Voices, which advocates for the over 60s, argues that  internet-based services are less reliable and much more costly. Poorer households are already cancelling streaming services because of the cost of living crisis. Protecting Freeview will prevent millions of older people and other vulnerable groups, at risk of loneliness and depression, from being excluded from public information and entertainment.

Take action to tackle modern slavery in artisanal cobalt mining, Investigate, exert pressure and legislate to tackle modern slavery in artisanal cobalt mining. This could involve new regulation of the cobalt supply chain to tackle unethically sourced cobalt, and/or the regulation and certification of products that use cobalt similar to the diamond industry., If the UK Government is a protector of universal human rights this should be an issue the UK Government should be tackling immediately.

Create & Implement a full package of Online Child Safety for the curriculum, Current legislation is either non statuatory or the statutory Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education guidance does not go far enough to ensure that a standard level of education is created by proficient people to ensure a top level and consistent., I was medically discharged from the RAF Police in 2019 with C-PTSD after 6 years in a role where I had to analyse the imagery associated with paedophile investigations. I have looked into the eyes of children who have been abused and there is not enough being done to ensure that children are given the information they need to defend themselves or indeed parents to defend their children. As a society and as a government more needs to be done in this area as buzzwords and platitudes don't work.

Ensure GCSE students are issued equation sheets in 2024, We want the Government to ensure current Years 10s are given the form of formulae and equations sheets for GCSE mathematics, physics and combined science in 2024. This has been arranged for 2023, and we want it to also apply to current Year 10s., We want the Government to do this because we think that Covid-19 had an impact on everyone's learning and that having to learn all the equations puts too much pressure on students.

Publish mandatory curriculum content on online safety for children, The Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education statutory guidance contains content on internet safety and harms, but it is up to schools how to deliver this. We want the Government to require schools to teach a standardised course on online safety for children., I was medically discharged from the RAF Police with C-PTSD after being in a role where I had to analyse the imagery associated with child sexual offence investigations. Statutory guidance sets out what it expects students to be taught, but leaves it to individual schools to decide how to deliver this. This means children can receive wildly varying standards of education on the subject. We want the Government to commission a comprehensive learning package that all schools are mandated to teach to achieve those outcomes.

Uncap tax-free childcare, Nursery costs have risen so high that the £2,000 cap does not cover the cost of the tax on childcare costs, the Government should uncap this and make it fully tax free to help with the costs, Uncap the tax free childcare amount to help towards the costs of childcare. Although it’s not much it would help towards struggling families with the cost of childcare. Nursery fees for under threes have far exceeded the £2,000 cap. For it to be classed as tax-free childcare, the Government should uncap this to make the scheme fully tax free.

Do not remove LGBT content from the Relationships Education curriculum, We believe kids should learn about this at an early age. I am sure there are many parents who want their and other children taught about LGBT issues in primary school., There is a petition to remove this content, which we believe is discriminatory. LGBT people exist, they have the same rights as the rest of us and kids should know them and accept them without judgement or issue. Despite what their parents might believe.

Allow LGBT content to be taught in the relationships education curriculum., As a member of the LGBT community, I struggled to embrace it when I was younger because I wasn’t taught about it and what it meant. In this day and age I think it’s so important for children to learn and understand it., It’s important. A child being taught about it and not being taught about it can be the difference between an individual growing up knowing who they are and understanding it or growing up to be really confused and struggling to accept it. Taking it out of the curriculum is disgusting. It’s unfair how a partition has been made to get rid of it but not to keep it? You’re getting one side of the story and one side of opinions. It’s extremely important to a lot of people too.

Fund additional support for children during the EHCP assessment process, There is no difference in a child’s needs before and after an EHCP has been collated, so there should be no difference in the support provided. The Government should therefore provide additional funding to schools so that they are able to support children during this lengthy process. , As a parent of a 5-year old diagnosed autistic child I have experienced first hand the effect that lack of funding has on children awaiting EHCP. During this process I have met numerous professionals, other parents and children who are not receiving the support they need while an EHCP assessment is underway. Children are being put on reduced timetables for long periods of time or having to be educated in empty classrooms and losing education time with peers. It’s not good enough.

Require alcoholic drinks to be clearly labelled as vegetarian, vegan, or not, Many alcoholic drinks are made using Isinglass, a substance taken from the swim bladders of fish. This means many drinks are not vegetarian or vegan, but labelling is poor compared to other products. Please require manufacturers, retailers and hospitality venues to clearly label alcoholic drinks., As a result of poor labelling with regard to brewing processes for Beers, Ales, Wines and Ciders, many Vegetarians or Vegans who avoid animal products in their food and drinks do not have the information they need to avoid consuming products that contain fish guts (Isinglass). Clear and obvious labelling would allow Vegetarians (10% of population) and Vegans (3% of population) to be confident about their consumer choices when in pubs and restaurants. We are so often unable to rely on staff to correctly advise.

Ban rent rises for social housing during rising cost of living , As most people in social housing are in the lower bracket of income, a rise in rent is totally unreasonable and unaffordable with the current rising cost of living.
Most people like myself who have house issues wait months for the problems to get fixed. 
, The number of tenants is a lot greater than the number of staff these social housing companies have so I do not see what makes this rise in rent necessary. Even the rent on things like garages is going up. I rent a leaky garage and I am still waiting for the roof to be fixed and their answer is to put the rent up.

The PM and members of Cabinet should be required to publish their tax returns, Parliament should introduce legislation that would require the Prime Minister and all members of the Cabinet to publish their tax returns annually. Such a law would go a long way in restoring trust in our politicians and in politics more widely., The Prime Minister himself said before Christmas 2022 that he would be publishing his tax return but, at the time of writing, still hasn’t done so.  A law requiring the Prime Minister and all members of Cabinet to publish their tax returns annually would mean that we would not have to rely on individual promises.

Review and enhance the rights of Service Family Accommodation (SFA) tenants, We believe Armed Forces families are consistently let down by the service providers that are supposed to maintain Service Family Accommodation (SFA). We want the Government to review and enhance the rights of SFA tenants, so they have at least the same rights as private tenants., The Defence Infrastructure Organisation is responsible for holding service providers to account, but the families living in this accommodation often struggle to have issues with accommodation resolved. We want the Government to review the existing rights of SFA tenants, and ensure they have the legal right to personally hold providers to account where they neglect their responsibilities, just like a private tenant would.

Make it illegal for restaurants to automatically add gratuity to the bill, Many restaurants now value their own service by automatically adding a service charge onto the bill. We believe this is essentially a hidden charge that relies on socially anxious people wanting to avoid confrontation in order to make customers pay more., We believe automatically adding a service charge to the bill is an unfair extra charge on the customers. The  value of service should be at the discretion of the customer, not the staff. This extra charge is being paid by unwilling customers because they don't want to ask staff to have the fee removed. We think too many companies are being unduly greedy and taking advantage of their customers.

Legally recognise Emotional Support Animals (ESAs), I want Emotional Support Animals (ESAs) to be legally recognised as legitimate assistance animals, so they cannot be refused by public services such as taxis, buses and shops., As I know people with mental health issues that require Emotional Support Animals and the stress of their ESA not being allowed into places can be alarming and off putting, especially if you're emotionally vulnerable. I've personally experienced this as I've been refused by services for my Emotional Support Animal and it needs to stop now.

Make it compulsory for schools to teach about the British Empire, The Government should make it mandatory for secondary schools (optional for primary) to teach about the empire as part of the history curriculum., Curriculum content on the British Empire should be frank and honest. The next generation must know so we can move forward as a society.

Schools are currently not required to teach about the British Empire. That means many students remain oblivious to this shameful period of British history, allowing harmful misconceptions that it was beneficial to be perpetrated and “nostalgia” to develop. It cannot be ignored. It must be taught.

As children, many were raised by the media to feel proud that Britain had ruled so much in the past. We believe that was wrong, and the empire was wrong. But due to lack of teaching, few seem to understand that.

Require background checks and references for shared student accommodation, Create a law that requires landlords who rent single rooms in shared student accommodations to do criminal record checks and seek character references from previous landlords and employers., There are too many cases where individuals with backgrounds that make them unsuitable to live in shared student accommodation have been able to rent rooms in such accommodation. This can lead to the harassment and assault of other residents.
 
There needs to be more preventative measures in place to prevent this happening to more young people.

Make 'Care Experience' a Protected Characteristic, Looked after children and care experienced adults can face abuse and discrimination which the Government could help prevent by making care experience a protected characteristic., When a child comes into care, the council and government become their Corporate Parent, meaning that they are responsible for providing the best possible care and safeguarding for the children they look after. An essential element of this care should be the prevention of discrimination.
 
No matter their age, people with care experience will always carry the label of being care experienced. The Government should do what it can to ensure such people do not suffer discrimination as a result.
Make CPR a part of the school curriculum, Make schools require to learn how to perform CPR,

Introduce a national Childsmile programme for children in nurseries and schools, Tooth decay (dental caires) is largely preventable, and I want the Government to introduce a Childsmile programme for nurseries and schools., Help younger children with supervised tooth brushing at school, giving oral hygiene instructions, access to dental care, and supplying toothbrushes
 
There is already a Chidsmile programme in Scotland, to support young children and families by helping them care for their teeth. By introducing a similar scheme in England, we could see a reduction in the amount of tooth decay, emergency dental appointments, and admissions into hospitals for tooth extractions.
 
Implementing the same strategies as the Childsmile programme in Scotland could greatly benefit our children, families, and NHS dental services.

IBS hurts. Require manufacturers state what type of sugar their products contain, We want food and drink manufacturers to be required to include on labels which types of sugar their products contain, and the percentages of different sugars., Between 10-20% of people in the UK have IBS. For us, different types of sugars can have different effects. Sometimes even the ratio of one sugar to another can be important. Eating the wrong type of sugar can cause significant pain.
 
The majority of manufactured food contains sugar and the majority of food packaging only lists "sugar" without stating what type has been added, which makes trying new products a lottery. Where manufacturers are adding sugar, they should be required to state which type and in what volume to help people with IBS.

Update the Equality Act to make Neurodiversity a Protected Characteristic, The Government should add Neurodiversity as a protected characteristic to Section 4 of the Equality Act 2010: protected characteristics., People are neurodiverse may be protected under the characteristic of disability, and we want neurodiversity to be made a specific protected characteristics.
 
Neurodiversity is a subsector of Biodiversity that should be considered a protected characteristic.
 
People's capacity to operate within their environment is dependent on how adapted they are to it and how adaptable that environment is to them.
 
We want the Government to understand neurodiversity as a relationship between the individual and their environment (social, economic, political, physical, and cultural).

End age discrimination in Universal Credit housing cost entitlements, To make entitlements to housing costs equal for all ages, and not to be discriminated due to being under 35., A person of 24 can have the same housing costs as someone who is 35, but the 24 year is only entitled to the rent for a single room in a shared house.
 
People who get support with housing costs through Universal Credit are already on low incomes, without having to pay out on any rent that is not covered by their benefits. With the current price rises, everyone is struggling, meaning many people who are under 35 on benefits are struggling to pay their rent. This can mean people being forced into unsafe, and unfair living arrangements, and having to choose between food, gas, electric or a roof. This age discrimination to those under 35.

Make it law that public sector workers get an annual pay rise of CPI inflation, Introduce a new law requiring all public sector workers to receive an annual pay rise of at least current CPI inflation., On average, public sector pay has decreased by 4.3% in real terms between 2009 and 2021. This should not be happening.
 
Public sector workers have been striking for way too long. These are unprecedented times.
 
On average, public sector pay has decreased by 4.3% between 2009 and 2021. Almost the whole of the public sector is striking.
 
According to analysis of Office for National Statistics data by the Guardian, here is how much public sector pay has risen between 2009 and 2021.
 
1. Train/tram drivers 12.2%
2. Paramedics -2.8%
3. Police officers -13%
4. Secondary education -9.7%
5. Primary and nursery education -11.8%

Amend the list of ethnic groups and remove 'Black' as a label, The word ‘Black’ was a racial label created during the colonial era in the 17th and 18th centuries as a justification for forced labour, and enslavement of Africans. We want the list of ethnic groups used by Government to refer to specific ethnic groups, and not use 'Black' as an ethnic group., The word ‘Black’ was used as part of the social hierarchy formed by colonialism during the 17th and 18th centuries to deny privileges to non-whites and to justify the enslavement of Africans, who were considered black. We believe using 'Black' as an ethnicity, with all the negative connotations associated with it, in the modern, post-colonial era is wrong. We consider it derogatory, outdated and an unrepresentative label. Rather it should be African or Caribbean.

Legislation to protect children against racism & all discrimination in UK School, The Equalities Act 2010 is not protecting our children from harm. Historically there has been major concerns regarding racist discrimination in UK schools, in light of Child Q, Child A and many others that do not get publicity. We are calling on the government to put in place stricter legislation., Create a Safeguarding Bill specifically against racist discrimination in Schools. Do an investigation into Racism & bullying in  all UK school's.

Black children face harsher punishments often for defending themselves against racist bullying, schools are not reporting or acting on racism that children face on a daily basis. Schools should be a safe environment for children, however, they are not being protected. The equalities Act 2010 needs to be updated and schools have an ANTI RACIST & BULLYING BILL.

Include Creation Science in the National Curriculum., There is a lot of literature and research on Creation Science. The Government should consider its inclusion in the national curriculum in respect to the study of origins alongside evolution which is already in the curriculum., Children should learn about Creation Science. Currently it is kept within religious communities, but schools should be able to explore it in the classroom so that children can look at the information and make their own conclusions.

Make Catfishing a specific criminal offence, Take seriously the effects and outcomes this can have on innocent lives. People's lives can be ruined by catfishing, where a victim is lured into a relationship by someone using a fake profile. We want catfishing to be made a specific offence, so police and courts are empowered to tackle this., In the modern world we live in now, catfishing happens to too many people. It's not harmless but actually emotional abuse.

Too many people use fake profiles to pray on and emotionally abuse vulnerable people, take their money, pray on vulnerable people and cause serious distress.
 
My personal information, including photos of my child, has been used  by someone trying to catfish other people, and I have struggled to get any form of justice. It is essential the Government step up.

Increase funding to support individuals with eating disorders and their families, There is not nearly enough support for people with eating disorders, or their families. Many people struggle to access support, including through Community Eating Disorder Service (CEDS). More funding is needed to ensure that individuals with eating disorders and their families are supported., There needs to be more funding to support people suffering from an eating disorder, which can be deadly. Early intervention is essential to tackling eating orders successfully, but currently too many do not receive support early enough. We believe more training is also needed for medical professionals to ensure they are able to diagnosis and make suitable referrals for people suffering from eating disorders. It is estimated that around 1 in 50 people in the UK suffer with an eating disorder. Support for sufferers, and their families, needs to be improved.

Make school libraries and librarians a statutory requirement, Access to a school library and a qualified librarian should be the right of every child. Government should create a statutory requirement for every school to have a library and qualified librarian to support the development of learning and reading for pleasure., Evidence shows that reading for pleasure improves life outcomes, lifelong mental health and academic attainment and has a greater impact on children’s attainment than socio-economic background. Despite this, 1 in 7 primary schools in England don’t have a library. Many more have a library but no qualified staff. Libraries are a statutory requirement in prisons but not in schools and in an era where schools are chronically underfunded anything non-statutory will be the first thing to disappear.

Increase funding for all mental health services, We want the Government to increase funding for all mental health services, but especially Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), to improve services and ensure people can access the support and treatment they need., At present too many people struggle to access quality mental health care. This is a particular issue for children and adolescents. We believe increased funding is essential to improve the quality of and access to these services, to prevent the tragic consequences that can result if people don't receive the support they need.

Keep the BBC Singers and stop decimating historic, priceless arts organisations., Stabilise funding for the BBC without an atmosphere of continual threats, so that world-class ensembles such as the BBC Singers remain viable along with the ecosystem of professional and amateur music that groups like this support, The BBC Singers are unique as a salaried choral ensemble in the UK. They are as good as it gets and contribute to all genres of music across the range of BBC radio and TV output. Their loss endanger an ecosystem which includes schools and colleges, amateur and pro ensembles, teaching and workshops, the Prom concerts and on and on...

Improve mental health and neurodivergence services in the Humber, We need more funding for mental health & neurodivergence services in the Humber, & cooperation between these & local generalised services. This will provide adequate training & pay for new and current staff, early intervention (e.g in the workplace & educational institutions),  & specialised care., People who access routine care are being discharged and excluded. Those attempting to access emergency care are also being turned away (Mental Health Network). The mental health of the Yorkshire and Humber area is particularly at risk. For example, Yorkshire and the Humber have the highest suicide rate per 100,000 people (12.5) from 2018-2020 out of any other region in the UK. This statistic is significantly higher than the average rate in England (10.4). They matter.

Require secondary schools to teach about the risks of vaping, We believe that secondary schools should be required to teach about the risks of vaping, alongside teaching about the harms from smoking tobacco , Vaping has become more popular amongst many young people, and we think it is essential that children are taught about the risks of vaping.

Secure digital freedom: Enact a Digital Bill of Rights. Forbid CBDC, Enact a Digital Bill of Rights to protect individuals' biometric data, financial autonomy, and privacy from digital surveillance and psychological warfare. Secure the fundamental rights and dignity of all people in the digital age. #DigitalRights #Privacy #BiometricDataProtection, We call on the UK Government to enact a Digital Bill of Rights, safeguarding individual ownership and control of biometric data and prohibiting harmful digital technologies such as psychographic warfare. The bill must also protect against the use of central bank digital currencies, preserving individual financial sovereignty.

Fund 30 hours free childcare this April not over a rollout, The childcare changes need to come in April 2023 to help families sooner than 2024, families are struggling already and change is needed sooner rather than later.,

Begin 30 hours of free childcare to all children under 5 now., I want the Government to begin their rollout of free childcare for children across England between 9 months and 5 years old right now. As a parent of two children one of which is not yet 2 years old this will not help our family and countless others as we won’t be able to access these services., The chancellor announced that he wished to incentivise and help people return to work. The current dates announced for when these benefits will be introduced will help mostly future parents rather than parents who already have children between the ages of 9 months and 5 right now who desperately need support. Why even announce this benefit when it won’t actually begin to take effect until April next year.

Bring forward start of childcare for children over 9 months old., To start the new funded hours of childcare to September 2023. To ensure working families have the chance to be able to afford the significant cost of living. If the government task is to increase workforce and economic productivity then it needs to support childcare now., I would like the government to show now its wish to create economic activity and help women now with child care.
Although the government says its needs time to increase capacity it already has the infrastructure in place to pay nurseries. I propose 15 hours for all eligible family's of 9 month olds from 1st September 2023 and increase the amount paid to nursery's.
This also gives nursery's time to decide if they can offer it or not.
I would then suggest that 30 hours is offered from April 2024.

Increase funding for hospices, Hospices in the UK provide care to 225,000 people each year, giving families support throughout the most difficult times of their lives. These hospices rely heavily on the kindness of the public to donate in a range of ways to support the work. Therefore I am asking Government to increase funding., Many hospices do not receive any Government funding and the ones that receive money from NHS investment is often only a small percentage of the overall costs. I would like the Government to increase how much is invested into hospices. Increased Government funding for hospices should help secure the future of these services.

Increase bursaries for social work students, Bursaries for social work students has been frozen at the same amount for years, many since 2014. We want the Government to increase the amount of this bursary, to reflect inflation and increased living costs since they were last increased., Social work student bursaries provide financial support to students studying Bachelors, Masters, Frontline or Step Up Programme. We believe these bursaries are essential to the future and investment of future Social Workers.

Cap yearly rent increases for private tenants to average increase in pay, Legislate so private landlords can only increase rents by a maximum of average annual pay increases. At present there is no statutory protection from private landlords for tenants in what they can increase the rent by. The rental sector is in desperate need of help and more regulations of landlords., Please cap yearly rent increases for private tenants, and not just social housing.

Make it illegal to farm octopus for the production of food, Prevent the start of any form of octopus farming for the production of food to be allowed. Be a country which shows the world that this is completely unacceptable., Nueva Pescanova are a Spanish multinational company intent on starting production of octopus for food. We believe is abhorrent that highly intelligent sentient animals could be farmed for food.
 
As the world wakes up to food production and meat consumption, the start of this type of practice is literally going against the tide.
 
Octopuses are arguably as intelligent as humans and to see them bred and reared at this point of human evolution would be horrific.

Fund "Free" sessions correctly so nurseries give free childcare and be viable, I applaud the idea of free childcare ONLY if the full price is paid. The current scheme leaves a funding gap requiring the childcare provider to foot the bill for the gap …, or go out of business. Free childcare is not free! The "loss' is funded by the nursery provider, Fund nursery places properly.

The fact that the Government is erroneously promoting free childcare and legally tying up providers to bridge the gap and make a loss is catastrophic.  What other sector would accept being forced to offer their products or services at a loss?  

Effectively the Government is artificially controlling the business model and putting the sector at risk.

Stop schools requiring specific GCSEs other than Maths, English and Science, I would like the Government to make it so schools cannot require pupils to take specific GCSEs other than English, Maths & Science, even if the school is a specialised school. Allow all children to flourish in their chosen subject/s they love and wish to use throughout their adult lives., Education is vital to all aspects of life however each individual has different passions and skills. I think that children in an enriched learning environment where they are studying a subject, they have enthusiasm for are more likely to achieve higher grades and have better mental health. If a child attends a specialist school they should not be forced to take a GCSE that may not benefit their choices for further education or career choice, especially if the school was picked for the child at a younger age.

Recognise the National Unity Government of Myanmar, The National Unity Government of Myanmar (NUG), established in April 2021, consists of parliamentarians elected in the 2020 election., The NUG has gained staunch support from the people of Myanmar as evidenced by participation in campaigns such as silent protests. In October 2021, the NUG was formally recognised by the EU and French Parliaments. We urge the UK Government and Parliament to recognise the NUG as the legitimate government of Myanmar. This is vital to restore democracy in Myanmar.

Introducing Romanian Language in the GCSE Curriculum, We urge the Government and Parliament to incorporate the Romanian language into the GCSE curriculum as an optional course. This inclusion will foster cultural understanding and provide students with valuable language skills, benefiting them in their education and careers., Incorporating Romanian into the GCSE curriculum shall forge indelible cultural bonds, bestowing students with invaluable linguistic prowess for a boundless future. As UK-Romania alliances flourish, mastering Romanian emerges as a monumental advantage across multifarious domains. By reshaping the GCSE curriculum, students shall seize the epic opportunity to learn the Romanian language, celebrating our intertwined legacies.

Fund increased research into MCAS, PoTS and EDS and improved patient care, Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS), Postural tachycardia syndrome (PoTS), Ehlers-Danlos syndromes (EDS) are chronic conditions that can be debilitating. However, too many people with these conditions don't receive the support they need. We want increased funding for research and patient care., There is too little awareness of these conditions, meaning they can go undiagnosed, and patients not receive the care they need. However they are very real and a lot of people are very sick!
 
Please try to make the lives of people with these conditions easier by providing additional funding for research into these conditions, and to improve patient care.

Requirement for a cultural centre for the Spanish-speaking community, According to statistics there are more than 200.000 Spanish speaking people living in South London alone where they live in precarious situations due to the high cost of living and in a delicate situation and oca community kitchen has been linking food aid and free education for 3 years, Oca Community Kitchen sees the need in the community. Lambeth and Southwark are boroughs very much affected by this whole life impact. We require a building community  centre where we will provide a range of activities and workshops for families based on the full range of education to get young people off the streets and food aid to help them adapt to the day to day life and to be able to access better working conditions.https://ocacommunitykitchen.uk.Onehand helps another hand priority

Increase the 7-day period for stray dogs, cap kennel fees and offer instalments, The 7-day period after which a stray dog goes into council care needs to be extended as sometimes it may not be enough time for an owner to be aware and/or travel to collect their dog. Kennel fees need to be capped as some council/contractor fees are extortionate and payment plans aren't offered., There are many reasons an owner may not realise what council their missing dog has been picked up by and also may miss an initial call. Some councils use contractors and both council/contractor fees can be extortionate, which can result in an owner losing their beloved dog if they cannot pay. We want to see a fee cap and a requirement to offer payment plans. It isn't always an owner's fault why a dog goes missing.

Remove and ban the television programme “Naked Education”, Remove this programme.

It is disgusting, grown adults voluntarily getting naked in front of kids on television, potentially being viewed by millions of people is morally unacceptable.,

Add ballet to the national curriculum for primary schools, I want to change the way people, and especially boys, think about ballet, and make ballet accessible and inclusive for everyone., I would like the Government to add ballet to the national curriculum for primary schools, so that all schools have to teach this.
 
The main reasons I want this to happen are:
 
1. Teaching everyone ballet this should reduce the risk of individuals who want to learn ballet being bullied.
2. Ballet can help teach discipline encourage physical fitness.
3. Ballet could support progress in other subjects (music, PE, art and drama).
4. Putting ballet on the national curriculum would make it accessible and inclusive for everyone, no matter your background or ability.

Review use of BMI in diagnosis and treatment of eating disorders, We are concerned people are not receiving the correct help for eating disorders, due to their BMI showing them as being a "healthy weight". This can mean that eating disorders go undiagnosed and untreated. Reliance on BMI also fails to acknowledge that eating disorders are mental health conditions., I was diagnosed with anorexia in February 2023 but only received the help I needed on my third admission to hospital when my heart rate dropped to a dangerously low level in April 2023. I reached out for help in November 2022 but as my BMI is ranked as "healthy" I was not categorised as needing immediate help. As a gymnast I have a lot of muscle mass hence why my BMI is regarded at this level, disregarding the fact my condition was worsening. The use of BMI is an outdated measure of individuals.

Fund research into and increased awareness of Depersonalisation Disorder, More research into the condition needs to be done. Awareness of this disorder also needs to be increased, especially for clinicians. Research should look at how treatment options for sufferers can be improved., Depersonalisation Disorder, is among the most common yet under-recognised psychiatric conditions in the world. Little research has been done on this disorder although it affects millions of people worldwide. Research in Britain and the US has found that DPD could affect around 2% of the population – that is, around 1.3 million people in the UK, and 6.4 million in the US. Given the scale of the problem, more research on the disorder is needed. It can be a crippling condition.

Increased funding support for Avoidance Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID), The Government should fund increased NHS support for sufferers of Avoidance Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID)., ARFID is characterised by the person avoiding certain foods or types of food, having restricted intake in terms of overall amount eaten and sensory processing issues around Food.

ARFID can have a significant impact on a person's physical and mental health, but in too many areas sufferers do not receive the support they need. The Government should provide funding to increase NHS support for sufferers of Avoidance Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID), also increase funding of educational courses for NHS staff to help them gain a better understanding of ARFID.

Increase resources for HMRC to improve customer service, HMRC’s customer service performance has declined and this causes significant problems for taxpayers and agents. We believe delays to Making Tax Digital and plans to move more enquiries to digital channels mean additional resources are needed to provide the country with an effective tax service., HMRC has reduced its customer service staff numbers from 25,500 to 19,500 and we believe HMRC needs additional resources to meet demand. Whilst we welcome HMRC's move to online services, we are not convinced this will happen fast enough and are concerned vulnerable individuals may be left behind. There will always be a demand for traditional channels and the service level can be improved with extra resources.

Introduce Romanian Language GCSE and A-Level Qualifications in the UK, We wish to see the Government advocate for, and encourage, the approval of Romanian Language GCSE and A-Level qualifications. Particularly, the Government should provide support in liaising with schools and exam boards to provide a comprehensive report on the demand for such qualifications., Over the past decade, many Romanians have moved to the UK. The 2021 Census shows 472,000 Romanian speakers in England and Wales. Many Romanians intend to settle in the UK for the foreseeable future, and have their children attending school in the UK. It is only natural to request formal teaching support for the preservation and perfection of the language abilities of these children, encouraging reading, writing, and speaking excellence.

Require Local Housing Allowance rates be increased in line with inflation, We want the Government to require local authorities immediately increase Local Housing Allowance rates by 10.1%, to cover recent inflation, and then increase these rates by inflation every year., In the cost of living crisis many private tenants have seen their rents rise at a massive rate, meaning the LHA doesn't cover their rent costs and leaving many households in financial hardship.
 
Many landlords have had to increase rents to cover the increases in their mortgages, causing instability for both the tenants and landlord.
 
Most benefits have increased by 10.1% and is vital that LHA rates are increased in the same way, to prevent people being evicted because they can't afford their rent.

Ban artificial sweeteners from food and drink products, We want the government to ban aspartame and other artificial sweeteners from drink and food products. There have been some studies that show that it could have an adverse effect on consumers.,

Nationalise private rental properties, Buying homes to let as 'investment opportunities' can contribute to rent rises linked to mortgage rates. This can severely disadvantages people who rent their homes - they can be prey to extortionate rent rises and insecure tenancies., The housing crisis is particularly felt in the rental sector and despite regulation there are far too many stories of people exploited by unscrupulous landlords. I would like to see the Government nationalise the private rental market to ensure a consistent standard of housing and equitable rents which could make homes affordable and secure for low income families.

Create a Government exam board to make new language GCSEs based on census data, Currently, it is up to exam boards what language GCSEs to produce. We want the Government to create its own exam board to produce new language GCSEs based on the main languages of UK residents, using census data., Over the past decade, some communities have vastly expanded in size in the UK. Many people who have settled in the UK now have their children in school here. We believe it is vital for there to be language GCSEs for communities present in large numbers the UK. For example, whilst we have a Polish GCSE, and rightly so, the Romanian Community, which the latest Census puts at 472,000 speakers, has no such provision. It is only just that the Government brings in a mechanism to rectify this in good time.

Ban estate agents and rental websites from charging fees to view properties, The government should be taking action to help renters deal with the housing crisis. One way in which they could do this is by making it illegal for estate agents and rental/ flat sharing websites to charge prospective tenants to guarantee a viewing of a property they are interested in.  , The UK is going through a housing crisis, people are struggling to afford their rent and their living costs so adding on an extra fee in order to gain access to viewing housing without any promise of being accepted for that property is completely unfair.

Stop landlords refusing potential tenants because they claim benefits, Too many landlords are refusing to let properties to tenants who are claiming benefits, or are not in full-time work. This can prevent vulnerable men, women and their families from accessing appropriate accommodation, and should not be allowed., Local authorities are unable to house everyone in need, and waiting lists for accommodation can be extremely long, so many benefit claimants have to find privately rented accommodation, but can struggle to find a landlord willing to rent to a benefit claimant.
 
The Government must stop landlords from being able to refuse potential tenants because they claim benefits.

Make 'None of the Above' an option on all ballot papers, We believe it is our duty to vote as many people died in order to secure us the privilege. The only way I can express my view of election candidates is to spoil my ballot paper. I feel that there should be a box which allows me to vote for 'none of the above', which will reflect my feelings., We want 'None of the Above' put on the ballot paper, so this is included in the vote count and everyone can see how many people have voted for this and to give a true figure of how many people don’t want to vote for any of the listed candidates.

Ban homework except for GCSE coursework, We want schools to be banned from setting homework, except for GCSE coursework, which should be kept to a minimum., Because pre-teens and teenagers should be free to do more creative things with their spare time, or socialise with peers, or rest. Many students already have a stressful life and homework can add to this. Too much stress can effect work in school. We also believe that homework is not an effective way for students to learn, and often it is just used to recap what they already understand.

Increase cultural diversity in the national curriculum,  
We want more cultural diversity in the national curriculum to widen students' knowledge about the world they will be going into in the near future. The Government needs to show that we are a multicultural society through what the young people are taught. Show that the future is bright.
, Education is a key part of many people's lives; the gateway to their future. However, as much as it is useful to know about the past and the wonderful Shakespearean literature, we also need to be aware of the new emerging things in our society. The UK prides itself in being a multicultural society but there is not enough mention of other cultures in the materials that students are taught. The Government is responsible for the national curriculum, and should ensure this includes culturally diverse content.

Ban full repairing and insuring (FRI) leases for commercial properties, Under full repairing and insuring (FRI) leases the tenant is responsible for the cost of all the repairs and upkeep of the property and also the cost of buildings insurance. We believe this is unfair, and landlords should not be able to make tenants responsible for their properties., Please stop landlords taking advantage of tenants and independent businesses and ban full repairing and insuring (FRI) leases.

Give the CAA powers to fine airlines for breaching consumer laws, We want the Government to establish a legislative framework to allow the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) to heavily fine rogue airlines which trample over consumer protections. The CAA should be able to impose fines itself, rather than needing to take enforcement action through the courts., Thousands of people in this country are routinely denied their rights each year through unfair tactics by major airlines. For example, the right to be re-routed is often made impossible to make use of.
 
The CAA has routinely threatened legal action against major airlines for breaching consumer laws, but we believe that at present there is no clear and effective deterrent.
 
Large corporate businesses should abide by the same laws as everyone else. We believe the threat of large fines would incentivise them to comply with consumer law.

Add British Sign Language to the national curriculum, We want the Government to add BSL to the school curriculum by making it a core subject for all students. British Sign Language is used by around 150,000 people, and being able to communicate with BSL users is important., BSL is a useful skill to learn and master. This skill can be give great jobs opportunities as well such as; Teacher of the Deaf, Speech and language therapist, Sign Language Interpreter, Social Worker for the deaf, and Communication Worker (£27,303). The skill of knowing BSL not only means you can communicate more accessibly but gives you more job options.

Ban the display of calorie information on menus, adverts and front of packs, We want a ban on calorie information, including traffic-light labels, from adverts, menus and front of pack labels. I'm aware that this information needs to be available, especially to people with certain health conditions, but it can be available on request in restaurants, on the back of packaging., This could benefit people who struggle with eating disorders. Many of us with eating disorders can latch onto numbers, triggering negative thought patterns, filtering down to harmful behaviours that potentially put lives at risk.
 
People desperately fighting eating disorders are constantly faced with barriers, such as calories on food packaging or menus, which can make it difficult for us to make healthy choices and take small steps towards recovery, which are vitally important for our physical and mental health.

Change the law to guarantee NHS dental care for residents in England, The law should be changed to guarantee that all residents in England can have adequate access to a local NHS dentist., Many people in England cannot afford to pay for private dentistry. Since the start of the first lockdown, it can be very difficult for many people to get a dental appointment, even for those already registered with a dentist, and it can be difficult for many others to find or make a new registration with a NHS dentist. It's time the government shows that we, the people of this country who pay our taxes, matter.

Soft drinks and beverages should state milligrams of caffeine on their packaging, The law changed not too long ago now to have to be 16 or over to buy an energy drink. However, many drinks contain caffeine and for people who are also having caffeine in other drinks (tea, coffee or even effervescent tablets)., It can very quickly add up to more than the 400mg limit a day for the average person. I believe this would help people know more about caffeine in their drinks.

Scrap the sugar tax, Companies are reducing the sugar in their drinks and adding sweeteners to make sure they don’t have to charge extra. I am allergic to sweeteners., I’m not the only one in the UK who is allergic to sweeteners who would like to have a non-alcoholic drink when they go out without having to go through every option to find that all they can have is water. Companies are adding sweetener to drink and it’s changing the flavour that we all love.

Increase funding and support systems for mental health services and education, Improve access to mental health services
Address stigma and discrimination
Focus on early intervention and prevention
Enhance support for vulnerable populations
Collaborate with community organizations
Improve coordination between health sectors
Evaluate/reform existing legislation, The pandemic, cost-of-living crisis, wage stagnation and underfunding of mental health (MH) services has created the worsening conditions for MH sufferers up and down the country.
An increase in funding for early intervention and prevention will decrease the strain and cost of this crisis on the NHS and MH charities at a later stage.
Failure to address these issues early on has the potential for increases in crime, addiction, obesity etc which cost the gov't and NHS more in the long term.

Review aftercare provided by the NHS for everyone affected by a Cardiac Arrest, At present, there is no formal care pathway for Cardiac Arrest Survivors. We want the Government to review NHS aftercare for all survivors of Cardiac Arrest, to ensure they receive the care and support they need., NHS England has a National Stroke Programme that covers stroke rehabilitation, and NICE guidance (NG185) covers rehabilitation for a heart attack (and other acute coronary syndromes). Currently, there is no minimum level of follow up for Cardiac Arrest Survivors, meaning many patients are missing out on vital services helping them to a full recovery.

Resuscitation Council UK (RCUK) wants to improve the standard of care offered to all survivors and their key supporters by publishing a Quality Standard which must be made equally available to all. We believe a programme, targeted to the individual’s needs, would improve quality of life, be cost-effective, and may reduce hospital readmissions.

Introduce specific restrictions on displaying swastikas and other Nazi symbols, We call upon the Government to place strict restrictions on the display of the swastika and other symbols associated with the Nazis, such as the lightning bolts symbol of the SS, except when used in legitimate religious contexts, and in movies, games, museums and education., The swastika is an ancient symbol, but is most associated today with the Nazis and Neo-Nazis groups. Other symbols were and are also used by these groups.

Displaying a Nazi symbol in public can cause distress and lead to public disorder, and is deeply disrespectful to the millions of people murdered by the Nazis during the Holocaust and Second World War.

We can see the effect of this in the United States, were Neo-Nazi groups can legally use these symbols to intimidate and advertise their hate.

Exempt Autistic and Neurodivergent people from the bedroom Tax, Exempt Autistic and Neurodivergent people from the bedroom tax  so they can have accommodation that better suits their needs., Due to the bedroom tax and lack of suitable housing many noise sensitive Autistic and Neurodivergent people who live alone have no chose but to live in one bedroom flats which may not be sound proof. This can lead to distress and anxiety when other residents, who live above or below go about their day lives. If Neurodivergent people are Exempt from this they could live in available two bedroom houses that better suit there needs. If there is no one bedroom options available.

Limit commercial rent rises and increase landlord liability for business rates, To stop landlords inflicting extortionate rents on hard-working shopkeepers and killing our high streets, I would like to see the Government place limits on how much landlords can increase rents at rent reviews. 
, Also, to encourage landlords to work better with tenants and keep their properties full, I would also like to see landlords liable for 100% of business rates for vacant premises from the day they are vacated. I have been in business for 15 years now and was subjected to a 48% rent increase in 2018. My lease expired in 2022 and in order to renew it’s going to cost me a whooping 68% increase. At the new proposed rent my business is not viable, so I closed my doors for good on May 31st 2023.

Require consideration of family as part of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, This petition asks the Government to add a sixth principle to the Mental Capacity Act 2005 so that the family and familial relationships must be considered in the taking of an act, or making of a decision, under this Act., Allowing for close family relationships is the purpose of the new principle. It could help allow families to stay in contact with management in care homes and independent living homes, even though their relative is suffering from mental health issues and may not recognise them or want to be in contact with them. It should also help ensure that family members who demonstrate genuine care are able to check up on their loves ones.

Prohibit the publication of private addresses in newspapers, We want the Government to stop newspapers from being able to publish addresses. Currently some newspapers publish the addresses of individuals who have been arrested or convicted. This can put other people living at that address at risk. The Government should stop this.,

Review modern slavery laws to prevent use of child labour in chocolate industry, We want the Government to review modern slavery laws to prevent use of child labour in chocolate industry., We want the Government to ensure that companies which produce chocolate in the UK most be able to prove that child labour has not been used in the production process. If companies are found to use child labour, the Government should prevent them from trading in the UK. This will protect the consumer, as they can be certain that they are not unwillingly supporting a company that uses child labour.

Stop banks from deleting customers accounts without good reason., For banks to cancel customer accounts because they do not like the views of the customer or for any reason they cannot fairly defend in court is to make that person's or businesses's life untenable. Therefore there should be a lawton prevent it., In the modern world it is almost impossible to to live a normal life without being able to accept money by electronic transfer and pay for goods using a debit card. To restrict any business or person by not allowing them access to banking is a basic restriction of human rights that allows powerful organisations to wield power over their customers that is disproportionate.

Require labelling of all products produced by companies paying tax in Russia, We want the Government to require companies to label products sold in the UK to let consumers know that they pay tax in Russia. We believe consumers have the right to know if companies they are buying from contribute through taxes to the Russian Government., Russia is engaged in what is widely regarded as an illegal war against Ukraine. Taxes paid in Russia are helping to support this war. Some brands are continuing to supply products to, and pay tax, in Russia. 

We would want this rule to be UK wide and for companies who fail to correctly label their products to incur fines. We believe this measure could help decrease money going to the Russian Government.

Require warning labels on soft drinks showing sugar content, I am asking that the Government requires health warnings on all soft drinks sold in the UK, showing how much sugar they contain. Sugar can lead to tooth decay and weight gain. Warning consumers of sugar content to could help improve people's health and reduce pressure on the NHS., I lost all my teeth at a young age due to drinking soft drinks. I was never warned about how much sugar is in soft drinks, and think this should be clearly labelled on soft drinks.
 
To help protect public health, lower the burden on the NHS and save taxpayers' cash, as soft drinks lead to tooth decay and increase risk of a range of health conditions, requiring health warnings on all soft drinks sold in the UK could help to lower the risk of people suffering from tooth decay and other health conditions in the future.

Make it compulsory for schools to offer GCSE and A-Level Music., We ask that it be made mandatory for schools to offer Music at GCSE, A-Level and as an option in the English Baccalaureate. The International Baccalaureate includes Music, however the English Baccalaureate doesn't and currently schools can opt not to offer Music at GCSE or A-Level. , During covid many people turned to music, but since then, we think that music has become overlooked and undervalued. In an age where awareness for mental health is high, and given the benefits that music can have on mental health, we think it should be prioritised more as a subject and made available to study for as many people as possible.

Many countries have strong, well-funded music programmes that are supported by a national belief in the value of music education. For example, music education thrives in countries like Sweden, Finland, Norway and Denmark, where it often extends beyond the classroom to include extra-curricular musical instruction that is publicly subsidised.

Reform language and categories regarding ethnic heritage on Government forms, I want the Government to stop using the phrases "ethnic minority" or “ethnic groups” on forms, and only refer to "ethnic heritage" instead. We also want specific ethnic categories for people who are Black British, Asian British, etc, to recognise that they are British., I want the Government to do so as their forms and terminology are outdated. The term minority to me implies I am less than, which I am not. I was born in the UK. I am more British than my heritage but because of an outdated system I am often defined by my heritage rather than the fact I am British.
 
This is an institutional thing that I believe causes divide, and must be changed. Only the Government can do it hence this petition for change.

Introduce a Suicide Prevention Act to seek to minimise suicides, We want the Government to legislate to:

- Create a National Suicide Prevention Office
- Require suicide prevention plans, frameworks and training for public and private organisations
- Support statutory local suicide prevention partnerships
- Enable sharing of data on suicide deaths/attempts, - Require suicide prevention impact assessments for new legislation and policies
- Require lived experience input in developing suicide prevention plans and policies
- Establish dedicated crisis support and community support hubs
- Create provisions to tackle loneliness and social isolation
- Require the teaching of suicide prevention in schools
- Amend building regulations to 'design out' suicide risks
- Establish dedicated trauma and loss counselling
- Require RIDDOR reporting for suspected suicides and psychological injuries at work

Lobby UK BTL lenders/  banks/ funders & the Financial Conduct Authority., Landlords & investors are finding it almost impossible to refinance existing properties, or indeed purchase new BTL properties, which is stifling the investment sector and more importantly the surrounding industries related and reliant on the UK BTL market., The property sector is an integral part of the economy, this problem is not specific to landlords/ investors, for example builders, carpenters, plumbers, electricians, architects, planning consultants, builders merchants, estate agents, mortgage Brokers, Insurance Brokers. The increased costs with owning BTL property will ultimately be passed onto to the hard-working people that rent in the UK. In may also lead to a temporary shortage of available housing, something nobody wants to see happen. We need creative and decisive action to be taken immediately by the government and UK banking sector.

Make the teaching of Black history compulsory in primary and secondary schools, I would like the Government to require schools teach Black history as part of the national curriculum, to ensure students receive a culturally diverse education. Black history shouldn't just be acknowledged in its month, October, but should be a core part of the curriculum., I would like the Government to take action so that Black history is taught to our future generations. This could help increase the confidence in the Black community and foster a more positive social environment.

Make expressive arts more important in UK schools curriculum, At the moment, the expressive arts aren't considered very 'important' in schools. At my school, we have 4 hours of expressive arts out of 50 hours of lessons per fortnight. We need more expressive arts - it helps people who might not be academic to express themselves., The expressive arts can give so many young people opportunities. It's not like it's not important. So many people get a good well-payed career out of it. Think about actors, musicians, artists. Expressive arts need to be considered as important as maths, English and science.

Require daily sessions on mindfulness/meditation in schools, To require schools to have daily sessions on mindfulness/meditation. This should include teaching children ways to reduce anxiety, self-love, boundaries, meditation, self-regulation, confidence building, and positive relationships. I believe this would help them learn more effectively., I have been teaching these life-long skills in schools for 6 years and now train teachers in mindfulness/meditation. Over the 6 years I have seen a rise in children's mental health issues.
 
I believe that children should be given time throughout each day to practice activities that help with their emotional development. If this was required in all schools I believe it would help children learn more effectively, and support them dealing with issues later on in life.

Make makaton and British sign language mandatory in all schools, I would like makaton to be a mandatory language to be taught across all primary schools and British sign language be an option to learn in secondary schools. This will help children to be all inclusive to other children and also help communicate with non-verbal and deaf peers., I think it's important as we never know when we will come across someone who is non-verbal or an individual is deaf. This will help children be able to communicate regardless and also helps end the stigma behind non-verbal and deaf individuals.

To review the sudden decision without notice of banning visa from Tier4 to Tier2, Applications that are already being processed prior to the ban date should be processed as normal and any applications made after the ban date should be stooped in accordance to the uk policy in effect., We want the parliament to accept the applications made before the announcement of change as the applicant paid solicitor fees, allocation fees fast track, allocation for submission etc. There applications are already in process stage. The applicants have made huge commitments with hard work to pay fees to solicitor and home office for there applications to be processed to find that there is a sudden ban. We would like the government to simply process and complete current submitted applications.

Ban the sale of energy drinks to under 16s, Change the law on energy drinks to ban them being sold to under 16s. Consuming these drinks can have an adverse impact on children's physical and mental health., It is important we protect our children. I have witnessed children as young as 10 buying energy drinks that contain addictive ingredients.

Rebuild The Crooked House Pub, Petition to rebuild (wonky) the 1765 pub after being damaged in a fire*

*Remek the pub so it we con ave' a drink and watch a marble roll up hill, This is a Black Country site of historical importance to the local community, it is devastating to see it being torn apart.

Require schools teach students about diabetes prevention, There is a lot of work going into preventing type 2 diabetes. The NHS runs a Diabetes Prevention Programme that identifies people at risk of developing type 2 diabetes and refers them onto a nine-month lifestyle change programme. We want schools to be required to run similar programmes for students., Change4Life was good at getting children involved, but there's so much marketing and advertising of unhealthy food that we think more is needed to reduce the risk of people getting type 2 diabetes. If children are taught at a young age they're more likely to retain information and make use of it as adults, which could help reduce the incidence of type 2 diabetes, and the need for later interventions. This should improve health outcomes and save money.

Fund increased healthcare provision for OCD sufferers, The UK has only one 24-hour care facility nationally, providing 10 beds for both Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) and Body Dysmorphic Disorder patients.

https://www.swlstg.nhs.uk/documents/related-documents/our-services/334-ocd-referrers-guide/file, Around three quarters of a million people are thought to be living with severe, life impacting and debilitating OCD here in the UK.

https://www.ocduk.org/ocd/

Studies have found that rates of suicide attempts in OCD could be as high as 27% and are successful in up to 1.4%.

https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bjpsych-open/article/resolving-the-discrepancies-of-suicide-risk-in-obsessivecompulsive-patients-a-review-of-incidence-rates-and-risk-factors-of-suicide-and-suicide-attempts-in-ocd/B07F6BA120B93572B83C3C8B5A744120
 
My son is another suicide statistic for 2023. Please look after your loved ones and help fight for adequate care.

Ensure better communication between student health services to prevent suicide, To have a joined up approach between Primary Mental Health Service and Student Mental health services so that vital information is shared and future suicides are prevented, My daughter lost her life through suicide whilst studying at University the Inquest was concluded by the Coroner that there was a lack of interaction between the two teams and perversely if you have more of a significant mental health need for care interaction between the two fades away, which may result in future deaths.

Include people with Long COVID in the Covid-19 vaccine booster programme
, The Government has launched an autumn 2023 Covid-19 booster programme for people over 65 and at clinical risk. , This does not expressly list people with post-Covid syndrome (Long COVID). Based on evidence of immune system damage and symptom exacerbation by repeat infections, we think they need to be eligible.

A comprehensive review of Long COVID (post-acute SARS Cov-2 syndrome) research, "Long COVID: major findings, mechanisms and recommendations", published January 2023 finds: "beyond the acute phase, reinfection with SARS-CoV-2 contributes substantial additional risks of all-cause mortality, hospitalization and postacute sequelae in the pulmonary and broad array of extra pulmonary organ systems". A 2022 study by UK patient charities found that 80% of Long COVID patients deteriorate on reinfection.

Review the powers and responsibility of landlords to prevent drink driving, I want the Government to conduct a review of the powers of and responsibilities of landlords, with the aim to prevent drink driving where possible., My 19-year-old daughter was heartbreakingly killed in November by a drunk driver, and I believe change is needed to prevent similar tragedies.
 
It is already an offence to knowingly serve alcohol to a drunk person, or to obtain alcohol for a drunk person on a licensed premises. A review should investigate how often landlords are charged for the above offences, and how often reviews of premises licences take place. It should also consider new powers that should be given to landlords under the law to prevent customers from drink driving, such as confiscating their car keys. This could help prevent drink driving, and the tragic consequences this can have.

MHRA Publish the Orange and Green Guides Online, with free access, We request that this guidance is broken down into relevant sections and chapters, converted to a readily shareable format such as a PDF file and hosted on a single webpage. The webpage should be free to access., This enhances accessibility.  Online resources offer enhanced and intuitive search functionality and embracing digital resources over printed materials supports the UK's environmental goals. 

This approach supports the MHRA's mission to promote public health.

It showcases the nation's dedication to fostering a competitive and transparent pharmaceutical industry, attracting international stakeholders who appreciate open access to authoritative guidelines.

Make Guru Poornima a bank holiday, Guru Poornima is the first full moon after summer solstice. It occurs in July or August. This day is celebrated with honouring teachers, Gurus and mentors, who have offered valuable life lessons or education. As a mark of our gratitude, Guru Poornima should be made a bank holiday., The word “Guru” translates to “dispeller of darkness.” In spirituality, a Guru dispels seeker’s ignorance. While in modern scientific culture, teachers and mentors share valuable knowledge enabling individuals to excel.
 
As such, the Teacher-Disciple relationship has been guiding humanity, as evidenced by several historic incidents that changed course of history for the betterment.
 
Because this tradition encourages people to level up and excel, we want the Government to recognise Guru Poornima by making it a bank holiday.

Make suicide prevention a compulsory part of the curriculum in Secondary Schools, Suicide prevention to become a compulsory part of the Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education curriculum in secondary schools. Ideally, an accredited Level 2 qualification should be accessible, free of charge, for all secondary school students., School staff should receive appropriate training in suicide prevention.

Require restaurants to include carbohydrate information on menus, We want it to be made a requirement that all menus at restaurants include carbohydrate content for every meal. This would help people with type 1 diabetes, who need to monitor their carbohydrate consumption., For those with diabetes, knowing the carbohydrate content of a meal is vital. This simple step would empower customers to make informed choices for their health. It should help promote health-consciousness and inclusivity.

6 weeks holidays needs to be lowered to 4 weeks, To put 6 weeks holidays to 4 weeks out a week of the 6 weeks at the Christmas holidays and a week on another half term, Because it’s to long of a break for children they become bored and out of routine! They need routine! It’s also too long for working parents to have to find childcare for the whole 6 weeks it’s expensive

Change curriculum for Key Stage 3 Mathematics to focus on every day maths, Maths should teach things like managing a household budget, basic profit and loss, interest rates, spreadsheets; the types of things used in everyday life and work life. 
 
, Content on technical maths, such as quadratic equations, geometry, trigonometry and Pythagorus shouldn’t be in the curriculum but could be taught as part of an optional GCSE.

We have two GCSEs for English: English language and English literature, there should be two for maths as well.

To adopt a False Statements Act criminalising lying in public life and justice, The U.K. should adopt an act making it a crime to knowingly and wilfully make any materially false, fictitious or fraudulent statement or representation in the course of any matter within the jurisdiction of the judicial, executive and legislative branches of government., Such an Act would be consistent with the Nolan principles of good governance, would reduce corruption and would enhance compliance with the rule of law and the principles of equality, non-discrimination, democracy and respect for fundamental rights.

Make lying in legislative, executive and judicial proceedings a criminal offence, A False Statements Act should be enacted making it a criminal offence to knowingly and wilfully make any materially false or fraudulent statement or representation in the course of any proceeding within the judicial, executive and legislative., The adoption of a False Statements Act would be consistent with the Nolan principles of good governance, and we believe would reduce corruption and enhance compliance with the rule of law and the principles of equality, non-discrimination, democracy and respect for fundamental rights.
 
It should thus help promote good, democratic governance and public trust in state institutions.

Require all NHS bodies to be managed by medical staff, We want all NHS bodies to be managed by medical staff, and believe the Government should make this a legal requirement., Particularly in light of recent tragic events, we believe there are too many cases where the concerns of medical staff have not been acted on appropriately by non-medical management staff.
 
The NHS should be run responsibly, but is a public service and should not be run like a business. We believe that having NHS bodies managed by medical staff will help prevent poor decision making, including concerns about patient health and safety not being acted on.

Increase funding for child and adult eating disorder services, It is important that eating disorder services have more funding in order to help prevent patients being referred to palliative care. These services can help people with eating disorder recover, and we are concerned that they are not sufficiently well funded., Eating disorders are extremely serious mental health conditions and anorexia nervosa has a higher mortality rate than any other mental illness. We are concerned that some eating disorder patients have been offered palliative care. While some patients are less responsive to treatment than others, that does not mean they cannot recover now or in the future.

Include the impact of the Covid-19 lockdowns on the RSE and health curriculum, Include education on the impact of the covid-19 lockdowns, and in particular the impact on mental health, in the RSE and health curriculum. This should help children better understand the impacts of these lockdowns, and including the impacts these may have had on their own lives and mental health., The impact of the covid-19 lockdown is further reaching than just the academic impact on children and young people. We believe it would benefit this age group to learn about the impacts on mental health and life experiences of these lockdowns, and the reasons for this. This should help children make connections between the way they feel and the environmental impacts which may have led to this.

Remove the Maths training requirements for social work apprenticeships
, I would like to have the maths requirements removed from social work apprenticeships, as this is a barrier to people becoming social workers. We need social workers.
, We have a shortfall in social workers already, and people may be put off from pursuing these apprenticeships due to the maths training requirements. There are people who may excel in this field if they were not put off by these requirements. Let's not lose those people.

Require phenylalanine be included in nutritional information on food and drinks, Ensure food and beverage companies include the phenylalanine amount and percentage in the content of food and drink labels. This should be added to existing requirements to list the amounts of fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein and salt., People with Phenylketonuria (PKU) cannot break down the amino acid phenylalanine, which builds up in their blood and brain, and can lead to brain damage.
